parts:
Hi again!

I see that inla.mesh.create(.helper) is prepared to build a mesh either
on a plane or on a sphere.
Is there currently a way of building a mesh over another surface?

I guess so, because of the existence of the function inla.fmesher.smorg,
that I think is related, and because I remember some pictures of 2D
surfaces embedded in the 3D space from some of the seminars.

Is there any sample code around to see how it works?

Thanks!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: inla.fmesher.smorg
parts:
The fmesher program used by inla.mesh.create only knows how to generate triangulations on planes and spheres, but the code for constructing SPDE models can handle any 2-manifold. The general manifolds we've shown were generated by deforming spherical meshes, either through radial deformation based on a random field generated on the sphere (via SPDE/GMRF) or as a full 3-variate SPDE/GMRF on the sphere.

Triangulations generated by other programs, or by hand can be translated into inla.mesh format by supplying both tv and loc to inla.mesh.create, where tv is a matrix of vertex indices for each triangle, in count clockwise order, and loc is a matrix of vertex coordinates, in R3.
For example, it should be possible to use the CGAL library to generate triangulationstand use with inla, but I haven't tried that.

parts:
Thanks Finn, If I could provide the triangulation manually it would fit my needs.

However, it doesn't work as I understand from your statement.
Here is a toy example with only two triangles:

# manual mesh 2D
mtest <- inla.mesh.create(loc=matrix(c(0,1,2,3,0,2,1,0), ncol=2), tv=matrix(c(2,3,1,1,3,4), ncol=3), extend=FALSE)
plot(mtest)

It keeps extending the boundary, even when extend=FALSE.
It gets solved by specifying a boundary.

# manual mesh 2D
pts <- matrix(c(0,3,2,1,0,0,1,2), ncol=2)
mtest <- inla.mesh.create(loc=pts, tv=matrix(c(2,3,3,4,1,1), ncol=3))

But I'm more interested in specifying a mesh over a (non-spherical) surface:

# manual mesh 3D
pts <- matrix(c(0,3,2,1,0,0,1,2,0,0,1,0), ncol=3)
mtest <- inla.mesh.create(loc=pts, tv=matrix(c(2,3,3,4,1,1), ncol=3), boundary=inla.mesh.segment(pts[4:1,]))

still complains about not being on a plane or a sphere.

Thank you again!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: inla.fmesher.smorg
parts:
Hi!

This is due to a lack of storage-mode-checking by inla.mesh.create.  The following modification should work:

mtest <- inla.mesh.create(loc=matrix(c(0,1,2,3,0,2,1,0), ncol=2), tv=matrix(as.integer(c(2,3,1,1,3,4)), ncol=3), extend=FALSE)

I'll add code to the package to make sure it gives fmesher an interger matrix for tv.  Thanks for the test cases...

Note:
When "tv" is supplied, "extend" defaults to FALSE, and fmesher doesn't actually honor "extend=TRUE" when given a full triangulation; the effect could instead be mimicked by constructing lots of "interior segments".  The only other current situation where extend=FALSE works is when a lattice or explicit boundaries are supplied; we've found a way of extending that to arbitrary planar point sets, but haven't implemented that in the package yet.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: inla.fmesher.smorg
parts: Your non-planar example fails only because of an oversight in the logic dealing with pre-specified triangulations.  fmesher cannot handle refining a non-R2/S2 triangulation, and bailed out without realising that you didn't ask it to refine.  I'll figure out a fix.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: inla.fmesher.smorg
parts:
A temporary workaround is to construct a mesh object with the desired triangles but planar coordinates, and then replace the vertex coordinates with the intended ones:

mtest <- inla.mesh.create(loc=cbind(matrix(runif(nrow(pts)*2),nrow(pts),2),0), tv=matrix(as.integer(c(2,3,3,4,1,1)), ncol=3))
mtest$loc=pts
